meta.title: Selekoa historical research sample
meta.scope: Selected historical records, 1965–2024, plus prior roles with unknown dates. Genesis source checks are dated 2026-09-17; personnel-continuity checks are dated 2026-09-18. Human source review pending. Not a current or comprehensive sector inventory. Governance version histories through July 2026, researched September 18, 2026; policy text is not evidence of implementation. Selected capital and compute records through April 2026; transaction stages do not imply current arrangements or realised spending. Targeted corrections dated 2026-09-25: one attributed claim accepted after explicit human source review; a second narrowly scoped résumé passage is human-reviewed. Other seed claims remain pending. Intellectual Lineage II adds selected oversight citations and agenda reception, checked 2026-09-25; all new records remain pending human review. Evaluation Institutions I adds bounded institutional and documentary records, checked 2026-09-27; new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted. Evaluation Ontology I adds four scoped engagement and institutional announcement seeds, checked 2026-09-28; no human acceptance or legal succession inferred. Schema 2.7 records each source's language; the frontier safety framework sources also record the nearest existing Internet Archive capture, checked 2026-10-03. A capture shows only what the archive held on its date and does not authenticate earlier bytes. Schema 2.8 adds quoted framework provisions, recorded absences, provision-level changes and the first contested assessments to the frontier safety frameworks collection, together with Meta and Microsoft framework families, checked 2026-10-03; provisions describe what editions state, not implementation. Schema 2.9 adds control-structure and external-commitment records; its first topic, California SB 53 as chaptered (enactment, 19 quoted provisions and four framework editions that link themselves to it in their own words), was checked 2026-10-04. A commitment or legal obligation is never evidence of compliance, and no record states that the statute applies to a named company. Schema 2.10 records assessments as questions posed by Selekoa rather than statements of a source, and dates an assessment by what it assesses, never by the publication window of its sources (corrected 2026-10-05). Schema 2.11 adds propositions and the first human-thought collection: located texts from 1863 to 2022 that articulate, contest or bear on propositions about machine intelligence, each with its role and register, checked 2026-10-06. "Earliest located" means the earliest text found by the recorded searches; no record claims a first use, an origin or an influence. Schema 2.12 adds a collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s documented arguments about common claims on advanced AI, 1996–2026: dated passages that state, contest or bear on 29 generically phrased propositions, with engagement, retrospective reports and context-only passages marked, admitted 2026-10-08 from a machine-prepared and machine-audited candidate pack. A record says what a text states, not whether it is right. The 2026-10-10 frontier-governance increment adds selected provisions of the EU AI Act as published in 2024 and of the 2026 Digital Omnibus amendments that bear on general-purpose AI model providers, and the New York RAISE Act as announced by the Governor; checked 2026-10-10, new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted, and Regulation texts describe duties, not compliance. The 2026-10-11 frontier-governance increment adds Commission guidelines, the training-content template, further chapters of the EU Code, a draft implementing regulation on proceedings, the New York Chapter 96 text and a Chinese generative-AI measure; checked 2026-10-11, new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted, and texts describe duties, not compliance. Schema 2.13 adds a collection on the economics of machine intelligence: dated passages from 1952 to 2024 that state, contest or bear on 19 generically phrased propositions about explosive growth and about how mainstream economics treated automation and AI, with each text’s source tier, model conditions and stated estimates, admitted 2026-10-14 from two machine-prepared, machine-audited and cross-family-checked candidate packs. A record says what a text states, not whether an argument or model is right. Schema 2.14 adds structured author names to sources for citation export, 2026-10-15: a cataloguing aid for splitting personal names, not evidence about anyone’s name. On 2026-10-16 the economics collection gained a third strand, admitted from a machine-prepared, machine-audited and cross-family-checked candidate pack: dated passages from 1998 to 2026 in which economists and economics venues state, contest or bear on five propositions about recursive self-improvement, superintelligence, existential risk from AI, developers’ incentives and economics’ own engagement with these ideas; a record says what a text states, not whether an argument or model is right. On 2026-10-17 the maintainer's disposition of two cross-family machine checks revised nine proposition records in the Yudkowsky and human-thought collections; all remain seeds.

claims.subject: sl4-2002-05-03-yudkowsky-0205-3551
claims.statement: The SL4 message “Re: supergoal stability” (2002-05-03) articulates Y24. Replying to Wei Dai on goal-system stability, he refuses to design Friendliness that would serve a programmer's propaganda and says the response to a project attempting a self-serving AI is to beat it to completion.

time.note: Archive author index lists the message as "Fri May 03 2002 - 16:38:46 MDT" under "Eliezer S. Yudkowsky".

claims.qualification: Premise addressed: Racing to be first improves the outcome. Closest SL4 wording to the take itself: he endorses getting a Friendly AI built before a self-serving project. The 'other side' is a project building a self-serving AI, not a rival state, and the premise that the builder controls the outcome is not asserted. In 2002 he endorsed SIAI building a Friendly seed AI first; he did not claim the builder controls the outcome by default. Rejected explicitly in 2023: "anyone talking of arms races is a fool" (TIME), which does not refer back to these messages. "This" means designing Friendliness semantics for propaganda, i.e. an AI serving narrow goals. Cross-family check: holds the racing premise for a Friendly-first project; no located later text explicitly retracts that conditional strategy, so said-it rather than earlier-self.
